renewal_summary: Fabrikam is an existing Hosted API customer up for renewal in March. They anticipate a step-function increase in LLM usage due to a Q2 rollout of an AI agent inside their support product. Main renewal theme: shift from reactive pay-as-you-go to a predictable annual commit with guardrails (clear usage definitions, invoice preview, and alerts for spend/run-rate). They are receptive to adding Dedicated baseline capacity for steady traffic but want the option to burst to Hosted API without surprise bills.
usage_profile_current: Workload mix (est.): 70% chat (streaming), 20% retrieval/doc-search (embeddings + rerank), 10% offline summarization jobs. Regions: mostly us-east with growing eu-west usage (new EMEA customers). Model mix: mostly open chat models with occasional higher-cost models for premium tier. Notable behaviors: frequent streaming responses; retries increased during Jan incident (customer flagged concern about double-charging).
usage_growth_forecast:
Customer forecast (from 2026-02-25 call):
- Baseline today: ~1.2B billed tokens/month equivalent (chat + tool calls) + ~45M embedding input tokens/month.
- Expected by May/June (post-launch): 2.0B–2.6B billed tokens/month (+65% to +115%), embeddings up to ~80M/month.
- Peak/event days: up to 2.5x baseline for 24–48 hours during product announcements.
- Key driver: expanding AI agent to all support seats; currently limited to ~20% of tenant base.
Internal note: treat forecast as directional; customer cares more about a spend cap / predictable unit cost than exact token estimates.
recommended_packaging:
Recommended renewal packaging (proposal draft):
1) Hosted API annual commit sized to baseline (anchor at current run-rate + modest growth buffer). Include published overage rate for billed_tokens and embeddings.
2) Add Dedicated baseline pool option for steady chat traffic (if they want stronger latency SLO + predictable throughput) with clear burst rules to Hosted API.
3) Optional: Redwood Optimize add-on for ongoing cost/perf tuning (batching/caching suggestions + regression alerts tied to their prompt set).
Positioning: “Commit covers your steady-state; overage handles launch spikes; Dedicated is for predictability/latency-critical routes.”
guardrails_and_terms_to_include:
Guardrails requested by customer + proposed Redwood stance:
- Meter clarity: invoice based on billed_tokens (not raw tokens). Provide examples for streaming partials, tool calls, and structured output.
- Retries/fallback: ensure idempotency behavior is defined; customer wants assurance they are not double-charged on server-side retries/fallback routing.
- Caching: disclose how cache hits are attributed (billed token impact) and where it appears in usage exports.
- Invoice preview: offer monthly invoice preview window and a dispute window with a documented escalation path.
- Spend/run-rate monitoring: enable console alerts for unusual day-over-day spikes; recommend internal thresholding (e.g., notify at 75%/90% of commit consumed).
- Change control: any metering definition change should follow change-control process (shadow-billing compare before impacting invoices) and avoid mid-billing-cycle surprises.
- Credits/discounts: follow standard discounting/credits policy; avoid open-ended credits; expiry and application order must be explicit.
pricing_notes_internal: Customer is not part of the self-serve pricing experiment cohorts (mostly sales-led enterprise renewal).
